options: A nearby star cluster inside the Milky Way
The nearest big galaxy outside the Milky Way
A nebula where new stars form
A comet seen every 100 years
questions.explanation: Andromeda (M31) is the nearest big galaxy to our own — a spiral about 2.5 million light-years away.
questions.misconception: It looks like a faint smudge, so it is easy to mistake it for a cloud or cluster — it is actually a whole galaxy of about a trillion stars.

questions.prompt: Compared with the Milky Way, Andromeda's shape is...
options: a smooth classic spiral with no bar
an irregular cloud of stars
a round ball of older stars
a ring with a hole in the middle
questions.explanation: Andromeda is a classic, smooth spiral — no central bar — while the Milky Way is a barred spiral.
questions.misconception: Because most photos are taken at an angle, the spiral arms can be hard to spot and the galaxy can look more like an ellipse.

questions.prompt: About how many stars are in Andromeda?
options: About one million
About one billion
About one trillion
About one hundred
questions.explanation: Andromeda holds about a trillion stars — up to twice as many as the Milky Way.
questions.misconception: Numbers in astronomy are so large that 'trillion' sounds made up — but a galaxy is an island of a trillion stars or more.

options: Two small galaxies orbiting Andromeda
Two planets of Andromeda
Two stars inside Andromeda's core
Two comets in the Local Group
questions.explanation: M32 and M110 are small satellite galaxies that orbit Andromeda, the way moons orbit a planet.
questions.misconception: Anything seen near a bright galaxy could be mistaken for foreground stars — these are genuinely separate little galaxies.

questions.prompt: What will happen when the Milky Way and Andromeda meet?
options: They will merge into one larger galaxy in about four billion years
Every star in both galaxies will collide and explode
They will bounce apart and stay separate forever
The smaller will be swallowed instantly next year
questions.explanation: In roughly four billion years the two galaxies will merge into one larger galaxy — a collision of crowds where stars rarely touch.
questions.misconception: 'Galaxies colliding' sounds like star explosions, but space inside galaxies is so empty that stars pass without touching.
